text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
NASA BORBA

- Police blocked municipal assembly evening celebration of the Yugoslav national team victory at the European basketball championship. The federal government organised a celebration earlier in the day.
- Bosnian Serb parliament speaker Dragan Kalinic called Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic to wait for the decision of the constitutional court about the dissolution of the parliament.

- The Bosnian Serb constitutional court will rescind president Plavsic's decision to disband the parliament and she will have to accept a compromise or leave her post, said a Bosnian Serb government source.
- Rains and hail will delay this year's harvest and reduce the yield by 10 to 15 percent, said Srbislav Dencic of the Novi Sad agriculture institute.
- Foreign tourists with hotel vouchers can get Yugoslav visas valid up to 30 days at all border crossings.
- Montenegro puts up for sale majority stakes in another 40 small and medium sized firms.
POLITIKA
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic promoted seven Serbian police officers to the rank of general on occasion of Serbia Uprising Day July 7.
- All 7,000 agricultural machines to be exchanged for produce under a programme for renewal of agricultural machinery will be delivered by end of July, said the head of the Commodity Reserve Agency.

- Yugoslavia has to start talks on the trans-Balkan gas pipeline soon, especially with Russia's Gazprom, if it doesn't want the pipeline to bypass it, said technical director of Serbian oil industry NIS Energogas Borivoje Vranic.
- Serbian parliament to continue the debate on the law on local self-government to which over 1,000 amendments were submitted.
GRADJANIN
- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic is expected appoint a new prime minister and form a government of national salvation by Monday, said a source close to the president.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic said Bosnian Serb Army General Staff statement equal to state coup. The Bosnian Serb Army has entered political waters on one side of the conflict, Plavsic says.
- Bosnian Moslem authorities still holding 240 Serbs in prison camps in Zenica, Pepelari and Begov Han, writes Doboj paper Svitanja, quoting Serb sources in Zenica.
- "We are not interested in the interpretations of others," Bosnian Serb Major-General Petar Colic says in comment to Novosti on crisis in the Bosnian Serb leadership.
- Montenegrin parliament to discuss government changes. Major reconstruction of the government expected in the fall.
- Begej shipyard of Zrenjanin launches vessel for German company.
- Fans demolished shop windows, cars in central Belgrade during celebrations of Yugoslavia's victory in European Basketball Championship. Police arrest 95 hooligans.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA
- Montenegro television board of directors appointed Milorad Djurkovic, a sports commentator, as the new acting editor in chief.

- Fifty eight members of the Democratic Party of Socialists main board, including all three deputy chairmen, asked president Momir Bulatovic to convene a main board session on July 11 to discuss the nomination of a DPS candidate for presidential elections in the republic.
- The Friedrich Ebert foundation and the German Information centre will open their offices in Podgorica soon, according to the Montenegrin Information Ministry. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
